_source: Bluesky trend display names (as in trend_relevance_examples.json, cut at 24 characters): 300 drawn at random from the 3,029 distinct topics the policy-relevance vote scores >= 0.5, and 147 more drawn from topics whose name contains an evaluative word (slams, backlash, scandal, mocked, feud, threat, woke, ...) so the loaded class has enough examples; that sampling list only chose what to label, every example is labelled by reading it. Plus the display names of the 350 trend_relevance examples (a random sample of all topics), so the neutral class covers the same subjects the loaded one does: without them a plainly named topic on a subject with loaded neighbours (an agency, a lawsuit) was voted loaded by topic alone. ' (Archived)' suffixes removed. Labelled 2026-10-15 by an AI agent (Claude) against _rubric, for trend_relevance's loaded-language gate.
_rubric: loaded = the name itself judges, mocks or characterises (backlash, slams, blasts, mocked, feud, scandal, gaffe, rant, grift, snub, regime, fascism, corruption or abuse stated as fact, hoax, rigged, woke, an advocacy slogan as a bill title), so quoting it would carry its framing. Neutral = a person, place, event, official action, product or topic named plainly, including attributed claims ('corruption claims') and proper names that happen to contain such a word (a wrestling event called Backlash).
